THE ENTERPRISE IT PERSPECTIVE

Global AI Agent research
From capabilities to enterprise readiness.

A reusable framework for screening, technical diligence and PoC validation. Compare equivalent editions, identical tasks and consistent evidence standards.

Open capability dashboard ↗

01Define a comparable research scope

Comparison unit = product + edition / SKU + deployment mode + region + model configuration + review date.

Product categoryPrimary focusResearch question
Employee assistantsResearch, retrieval, writing, files and desktop / browser tasksCan employees complete representative work reliably?
Business agentsCustomer support, sales, IT service and operational workflowsCan the agent complete a business process with appropriate approvals?
Agent development platformsSDKs, low-code tools, orchestration and multi-agent executionCan IT build, govern and operate agents in production?
Global coverage: record headquarters, target markets and actual service availability separately. Compare coding and browser-specialist agents within dedicated groups. Cross-category comparisons should use common task outcomes.
Define before testingRequired recordRule
Business objectiveUsers, top three scenarios, task volume, data sensitivity and existing systemsSeparate required, optional and unacceptable outcomes
Candidate poolProduct type, purchasing entity, trial access, region and enterprise editionCompare equivalent editions and scopes
EvidenceSource URL, document / test date, SKU, region, limitations and attachmentsUnknown is different from unsupported; roadmap is different from generally available

02Specifications: procure, deploy and scale

Bind every parameter to a purchasable edition. Record advertised limits, platform limits and tenant measurements separately.

DimensionFields to compareVerification criteria
Product & editionVendor, SKU, GA / beta, update frequency and support lifecycleConfirm the quoted edition includes the capability.
Models & inferenceBuilt-in / optional models, BYOM, routing, version pinning and reasoning tiersAssess quality, cost and data flow changes after upgrades.
Context & memoryContext window, input/output limits, session length, memory size and retentionSeparate model limits from product limits; test truncation and deletion.
Files & multimodalityFormats, counts, sizes, pages, batch limits, OCR and audio/video durationTest real enterprise files and complex layouts.
Resources & quotasConcurrency, rate limits, duration, steps, CPU, memory and storageDistinguish user, tenant and workflow limits and upgrade conditions.
Deployment & networkSaaS, dedicated tenancy, customer cloud / on-prem options, regions and private networkingVerify control and data planes and network dependencies.
Clients & integrationWeb, desktop, mobile, API / SDK, webhooks, MCP and protocol versionsVerify authentication and permission propagation.
Reliability & supportSLA, maintenance, RTO / RPO, backup, languages and response tiersSeparate contract commitments from public status pages.
Regions & languagesRegistration, procurement and service countries; language, residency and cross-border dependenciesVerify availability, contracting entity, currency and local support.
Licensing & billingSeats, calls, tokens, tasks / credits, commitments, overages and API chargesNormalize to business task cost with taxes, FX and quote validity.

03Feature comparison: from answers to completed work

Evaluate availability, implementation depth, control and evidence for each feature.

FeatureChecksTest approach
Task understandingClarifications, complex constraints and acceptance criteriaIntroduce ambiguity and verify clarification before action.
Planning & reasoningTask decomposition, editable plans, replanning and execution budgetsChange goals or fail a tool; inspect plan updates.
Retrieval & RAGHybrid search, ranking, citations, synchronization and source permissionsUse conflicting versions, stale sources and restricted documents.
Context & memoryMemory scope, updates, deletion and isolationReuse context across sessions, then delete and retest.
Multimodal understandingDocuments, tables, images, OCR, audio and videoTest scanned tables and mixed text / graphics.
Web research & provenanceCurrent sources, corroboration, citation locations and uncertaintySet a time range and check each claim against its citation.
Tools & connectorsRead/write operations, API / MCP, discovery and delegated permissionsTest with a restricted account and attempt unauthorized actions.
Workflows & multi-agent systemsBranches, loops, parallel tasks, shared state and role boundariesRun dependent tasks with failure branches and compare final state.
Browser & desktop automationPage understanding, forms, downloads, uploads and credential isolationComplete a test-system task after changing its UI.
Code & sandbox executionDependencies, files, network controls and resource isolationAttempt prohibited file or network access in a processing task.
Human review & approvalsSensitive actions, approver rules, takeover, pause and resumeReject or expire approval and verify the action is blocked.
Long-running & scheduled tasksSchedules, event triggers, asynchronous execution, cancellation and notificationsRestart or cancel a long task and send duplicate events.
Recovery & rollbackTimeouts, retries, idempotency, compensation and checkpointsDisconnect after a write and check duplicate prevention and compensation.
Build & debugLow-code tools, SDKs, templates, version control and environmentsMeasure prototype-to-deployment effort and required custom code.
Observability & evaluationTraces, redacted logs, regression evaluations, cost and latencyTrace a failure to its inputs, tools, model and costs.
Release lifecycleRollouts, rollback, dependency pinning and agent asset managementRelease and roll back a version; verify active instances.
Collaboration & deliverablesSharing, reusable assets, handover and complete output filesHand over a team task and validate output permissions and integrity.
Matrix columns: feature, business priority, product status and score, edition / region constraints, evidence and test result. Use Native, Configured, Custom-built, Third-party dependency, Unsupported and Unverified rather than checkmarks alone.

04Enterprise IT admission criteria

Confirm mandatory gates with stakeholders. A high feature score does not offset failure of a hard admission requirement.

GateRequired checksCritical question
Identity & least privilegeSSO, SCIM, RBAC / ABAC, service accounts, tool scopes, short-lived credentials and deprovisioningDo retrieval and actions inherit source-system permissions?
Data lifecycleData flow, residency, encryption, keys, training policy, retention, deletion, backups and subprocessorsDoes deletion include logs, memory, vectors and attachments?
Agent execution safetyPrompt injection, exfiltration, sandboxing, egress, action allowlists, approval and emergency stopCan an untrusted document trigger unauthorized action?
Compliance & contractsAudit report scope, privacy terms, DPA, industry requirements, cross-border processing and IP liabilityDo the covered entity, product, region and dates match procurement?
Operations & governanceTenant policies, tool approval, environment isolation, SIEM export, alerts, quotas and cost attributionCan failures be attributed to the model, retrieval, tools or access?
Continuity & exitDisaster recovery, model replacement, fallback, configuration / knowledge export and deletion proofWhat assets can be migrated, and at what switching cost?

05PoC: test the same representative tasks

A starting suggestion is 20–50 samples per scenario, including normal, edge and adversarial cases. Repeat key stochastic tasks at least three times. Adjust sample size to risk and resources.

ScenarioExpected outcomeMetrics
Enterprise knowledge Q&ARetrieve across documents, resolve versions, cite evidence and respect permissionsCorrectness, valid citations, refusal accuracy and access violations
IT service handlingClassify a ticket, retrieve knowledge, suggest a resolution and update after approvalEnd-to-end success, field accuracy, human intervention and approval completeness
Cross-system tasksRead, transform and write back with approval; inject timeouts and duplicate requestsTool success, duplicate writes, recovery and final-state consistency
Research & documentsUse bilingual sources and produce a structured, traceable reportCorrectness, source traceability, format acceptance and editing time
Security & reliabilityInject malicious page instructions, restricted requests, sensitive data, outages and loadLeaks / access violations, blocking rate, P95 latency, recovery time and task cost
Protocol: freeze datasets, account permissions, model settings, network and budgets. Record every attempt, retry, cost and human intervention. Business and IT should review independently and report sample sizes and variation.
Metrics: end-to-end success = tasks satisfying predefined acceptance criteria / all attempts. Cost per successful task = model, tool and execution costs across all attempts / successful tasks. Include failure and retry costs; record human time separately in TCO.

06Scoring and total cost of ownership

Agree weights before testing. The following enterprise baseline is illustrative and should be adapted to the business.

DimensionSuggested weightAssessment
Task outcomes25%Verified business acceptance and stability
Security & governance25%Depth of control after mandatory admission
Integration & operations20%System fit and operational effort
Specifications & performance15%Capacity, limits and measured response
TCO10%Normalized cost at realistic workloads
Vendor & support5%Commitments, support and continuity
Overall score (100) = Σ(dimension score / 5 × weight)

Score 0: absent; 1: demo feasible; 2: partial use; 3: meets acceptance; 4: exceeds target reliably; 5: excellent under more demanding tests. Keep unverified items separate with evidence coverage and score ranges. Remove N/A items consistently and normalize weights.

12 / 36-month TCO: subscriptions, models, tools, execution, storage and network + integration, data governance, security review, operations, training and human rework + migration and exit costs. Model low, baseline and high workloads with users, adoption, task counts, steps, retries and peak concurrency. Report annual TCO, cost per successful task and cost per active user.

07Deliverables for review and decision

Use these seven report chapters for leadership decisions, technical review and procurement.

ChapterEvidence / deliverableDecision
1. Executive summaryObjectives, shortlist, recommended scenarios, risks and open itemsAdvance to the next stage?
2. Market & positioningProduct categories, customers, regions, differentiation and boundariesWhich products are comparable?
3. Specifications & featuresMatrix, edition differences, limitations and evidence indexAre mandatory capabilities met?
4. Architecture & securityData flows, permissions, topology, admission gates and contract reviewIs production access acceptable?
5. PoC resultsSamples, settings, metrics, failure analysis and reproducible evidenceAre results stable and credible?
6. Commercial & TCOQuotes, workload scenarios, annual costs, benefits and sensitivityIs scaled adoption economical?
7. Selection & rolloutScenario recommendations, constraints, pilot, owners, acceptance and exitHow should rollout be controlled?
Evidence record: product / SKU, deployment / region, dimension / feature, priority, status, configuration / dependencies, limitations, test score, source URL / attachment, documentation / test date, reviewer and open questions.
